[[File:Twilek_privateer.png|thumb|right|200px|A [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] privateer]]
A '''privateer''' was a civilian ship or individual serving a governmental organization in a paramilitary role, or a member of its crew. Often basically legitimized [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], privateers would operate under a government contract known as a [[Letter of marque/Legends|letter of marque and reprisal]], giving their [[Captain/Legends#Civilian use|captain]] authority to harass, seize and destroy the shipping of another organization&mdash;typically one that was considered an enemy in times of war.

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] was known to use privateers to bolster its forces, especially late in the war. This might have also been a tactic to induce pirate forces to attack [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] shipping, drawing the pirates away from the CIS's own lucrative mercantile shipping networks.<ref name="TFUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

In the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] would hire a number of [[Rebel privateer|privateers]] to harass [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] shipping, a policy supported particularly by [[Ral'Rai Muvunc]] of [[Ordnance and Supply/Legends|Ordnance and Supply]].<ref name="IHB">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> The Alliance was hesitant to use privateers, as they did not trust the mercenary nature of the groups. After some initial trials, [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] approved a procedure that allowed various Ministries to issue letters of marque with Executive approval. The relationship between the Alliance and privateers was considered to merely be one of employee and employer.<ref name="AJ2">{{JournalCite|2|Rebel Privateers!}}</ref> The Imperials also utilized privateers, with [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] giving explicit permission for privateers to raid enemy shipping on his behalf, and the Imperial Military tolerated their actions in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] so long as they did not directly interfere with the Imperials' activities.<ref name="IHB" />

[[File:Privateers_for_the_Alliance_SoT.png|thumb|left|250px|A group of privateers employed by the Rebel Alliance]]
After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the use of privateers by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] shrank considerably, reflecting the increased size and status of the [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] under [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Ackbar]], who had always opposed their use. Many retired with their pardons and hoarded wealth, but some continued to raid shipping in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. Others joined the New Republic and continued operations against the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]].<ref name="AJ2" /> However, Imperial [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] and [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] started issuing their own letters of marque, and during the crisis of the reborn [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], the New Republic once more made use of privateers. By [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], privateering sponsored by the New Republic, as well as by the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]], was nearly completely phased out.<ref name="Pirates & Privateers">''[[Pirates & Privateers]]''</ref> 

Following the fall of the Empire, its scattered remnants suffered from moderate supply shortages, prompting a reliance on hit-and-fade tactics and interdiction of New Republic shipping. To support these strategies, several "pocket Empires" began issuing letters of marque, authorizing privateers—ranging from Imperial captains with raiding privileges to pardoned pirates—to disrupt enemy logistics. These Imperial privateers operated with fewer ethical constraints than their Rebel counterparts and were broadly encouraged to damage New Republic trade. However, the fragmentation of Imperial space meant that letters of marque were not always honored across rival territories.<ref name="Pirates & Privateers" />

Privateers were common in the [[Hapes Cluster/Legends|Hapes Cluster]], where they seemed to serve the interests of political factions in the [[Hapes Consortium/Legends|Hapes Consortium]]. [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Isolder]] famously went undercover with the crew of [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] pirate [[Grov Bricker]] to track down [[Harravan]], the Hapan privateer who killed his brother, [[Kalen (Hapan)|Kalen]].

[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] had once operated as a privateer, including a close encounter with [[Hapan]] naval forces on the edge of the Cluster.

Other governments that issued letters of marque included the [[Allied Tion sector/Legends|Allied Tion sector]] and the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality]]. Some corporations also sponsored privateer-like mercenaries, including [[Tagge Company/Legends|TaggeCo]], [[Santhe/Sienar Technologies]], [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]], the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]] and the [[Mining Guild/Legends|Mining Guild]].<ref name="Pirates & Privateers" />
